name: Tang Hai
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Bondex Supply Chain Management Co., Ltd. (海程邦达, SSE: 603836), Qingdao
profile: Tang Hai (唐海) founded Qingdao-based Bondex (海程邦达), a freight-forwarding and supply-chain logistics group set up in 1996 that listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange main board in 2021. He was chairman and general manager at IPO; the group now has 2,000+ staff, 80+ subsidiaries and covers 200+ ports, with a growing focus on semiconductor/electronics logistics.
interesting_fact: Bondex has pushed into semiconductor supply chains via its JV platform 邦达智联 and presented at the 2026 North American 3PL Value Creation Summit in Chicago; it was ranked 26th among A&A's 2026 Asia-Pacific Top 50 3PLs.
deep_cut_fact: Per the 2021 IPO prospectus summary, Tang has chaired Qingdao Haixinda (青岛海新达) since 2001 and has been vice-chairman of Qingdao port e-platform 青岛港易通 since 2014 - both Bondex associates.
notes: Low public profile; little personal biography online. Best route is the board secretary / securities office. Chinese-language outreach advisable. Not to be confused with Jiangsu Hichain (海晨物流).

name: Ma Xiaocui
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2016) jointly with Li Shifa as a source of wealth in China Logistics Property Holdings (中国物流资产, 1589.HK), the warehouse/logistics-park developer Li founded in 2000 (Shanghai Yupei group). No public source found describing Ma Xiaocui's role or relationship to Li or the company.
interesting_fact: China Logistics Property ran a network of logistics parks across 38 locations; in 2021 JD Logistics agreed to buy most of Li Shifa's stake and bid for more shares.
notes: Could not verify who Ma Xiaocui is (Chinese and English searches return nothing linking her to the company; Li Shifa's 2016 HKEX disclosure lists no spousal interest). The Hurun-listed wealth relates to the Li Shifa/Yupei stake. Recommend skipping or approaching via Li Shifa / Yupei group instead.

name: Zhong Baisheng
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Tempus Group / Tempus Global Business Service (腾邦国际, formerly SZSE: 300178), Shenzhen
profile: Zhong Baisheng (钟百胜) founded Shenzhen-based Tempus (腾邦), an air-ticketing and business-travel services group that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext as 腾邦国际 and expanded into travel, logistics and supply-chain finance. After a 2019-20 debt crisis the listed company was delisted in June 2022; his current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Control of 腾邦国际 changed hands three times within a year around 2019-20, ultimately reverting to founder Zhong Baisheng.
notes: Hurun listing (2015-17) is stale: the listed company collapsed under debt, faced litigation and was delisted (摘牌 22 Jun 2022). No current published contact found. Sensitive subject; likely a poor podcast target.

name: Vitaliy Haiduk
current_role: Businessman; co-founder of Industrial Union of Donbas (ISD); former Secretary of Ukraine's National Security and Defense Council (2006-07)
profile: Ukrainian businessman and politician (b. 1957) who co-founded the Industrial Union of Donbas steel group in 1995 with Serhiy Taruta and Oleh Mkrtchian, exiting around 2009-10 when Russian-linked investors took control. He served as Minister of Fuel and Energy (2001-02), Deputy Prime Minister (2002-03) and NSDC Secretary; Ukrainian media say he now holds interests including security contracting for hydro plants.
interesting_fact: An energy-sector veteran: he was First Deputy Minister then Minister of Fuel and Energy of Ukraine and holds the title 'Honored Power Engineer of the CIS'.
deep_cut_fact: Before politics he ran the Zuyevskaya electromechanical plant (1988-94), and he wrote a PhD on the economics of leasing and co-authored the 2000 book 'Problems and prospects of development of leasing in Ukraine'.
notes: Politically exposed person; 2024-25 Ukrainian media (UNN) carry unproven allegations about his current business links - handle with care. No published personal or office contact found. Alive status inferred from recent media coverage (no death reported).

name: Lin Zhenggang
current_role: Former major shareholder of Yihua Healthcare (宜华健康, SZSE: 000150); chairman of its subsidiary 众安康后勤集团 (per 2019 filing)
profile: Lin Zhenggang (林正刚) became a 5%+ shareholder of Yihua Healthcare (宜华健康, the former Yihua real-estate arm of Shantou's Yihua group) around 2015 when it acquired his hospital-logistics business 众安康后勤集团, which he chaired. He and brother Lin Jianxin acted in concert; by 2022 he held ~8.45% but pledged shares were being forcibly sold.
interesting_fact: His wealth came from hospital back-office/logistics services (众安康), an unusual niche, which he folded into a listed healthcare platform in exchange for shares.
notes: Hurun's 'Yihua Timbar Stock' label refers to his Yihua Healthcare shareholding. Very low public profile, no personal bio found. 2022 filings show forced disposal of pledged shares - wealth likely much reduced. No published contact; weak podcast target.

name: Eric Herd
current_role: Owner and chairman/chief executive, Farmfoods Ltd (Cumbernauld, Scotland)
profile: Eric Herd owns Farmfoods, the family-owned frozen-food and grocery discounter with 300+ UK shops. He turned a 1954 Aberdeen meat-processing business into Britain's second-biggest frozen-food retailer and has been a director of the group since at least 1993; the chain is now expanding by 20-30 stores a year, notably around London.
interesting_fact: In 2011 Farmfoods teamed up with Asda in an unsuccessful bid for rival Iceland, under which Farmfoods would have taken about 200 of Iceland's 800 stores.
deep_cut_fact: Farmfoods' roots are a 1954 meat-processing firm (Farmfoods (Aberdeen) Ltd) whose first shop opened in Aberdeen in the 1970s; by the mid-1980s it had only about 20 outlets. It proudly says its no-frills stores have 'no intention of winning any interior design competitions'.
notes: Described by The Grocer as reclusive and the Scotsman as publicity-shy; no interviews found. A younger George Herd (likely family) also sits on the board. Only route is the company's general contact form.

name: Leon Jesus Zamora
current_role: Executive Chairman of the Board and President, Auna S.A. (NYSE: AUNA); Co-founder, CEO and Chairman, Enfoca
profile: Jesús 'Suso' Zamora León is a Peruvian private-equity investor who co-founded Enfoca, the Lima investment firm that controls Auna, a Latin American hospital, oncology and health-plan network (Peru, Colombia, Mexico). He has sat on Auna's board since 2008, became executive chairman in 2022 and took the company public on the NYSE in March 2024.
interesting_fact: Forbes Peru named him to its 'Los 26 del 26' list of leaders set to shape Peru in 2026; Auna plans to invest US$500m in Mexico in 2026-28 and to develop EsSalud's Torre Trecca medical complex via a public-private partnership.
deep_cut_fact: Though a Peruvian investor, he studied industrial engineering at Mexico's UNAM before an MBA at Columbia Business School - a Mexico link that predates Auna's big Mexican hospital push.
notes: Goes by 'Suso' Zamora in Auna materials. IR reports to EVP Strategy & ECM Lorenzo Massart. Healthcare rather than energy, but Auna's hospital buildout is capex-heavy infrastructure.

name: Robin Clark
profile: Listed on the Sunday Times Rich List 2020 with property wealth (~£200m). Could not identify which Robin Clark this is or the property business concerned; no rich-list profile or press coverage found.
notes: Identity unresolved - common name, several searches (rich-list coverage, property press) returned nothing. Needs the Sunday Times entry text (company name/region) to proceed.

name: Brian E. Lane
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, Comfort Systems USA (NYSE: FIX); Director, Main Street Capital (NYSE: MAIN)
profile: Brian Lane has been CEO of Houston-based Comfort Systems USA, a large US mechanical and electrical contractor, since December 2011, after joining in 2003 and rising through regional operations to COO. Under him the company became a major builder of data-center and semiconductor-fab HVAC/electrical systems, with technology work reaching ~45% of 2025 revenue and backlog near $12bn.
interesting_fact: Comfort Systems' technology segment (mostly data centers) grew from about a third of revenue in 2024 to roughly 45% in 2025, making it one of the biggest picks-and-shovels winners of the AI build-out.
deep_cut_fact: A chemistry graduate of Notre Dame, Lane spent 15 years at Halliburton (leaving as Regional Director, Europe & Africa) and was also a Regional Director at Capstone Turbine, the microturbine distributed-power maker - real on-site power experience now relevant to data centers.
notes: Highly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast. Gave up the President title in Dec 2025 (remains CEO) - possible succession planning. Corporate general inbox is the published route; IR is handled by the CFO's office.

name: Jon Moulton
current_role: Private equity investor; founder of Better Capital and Alchemy Partners; principal behind Perscitus LLP family office (London/Guernsey)
profile: Jon Moulton (b. 1950, Stoke-on-Trent) is a veteran British private-equity investor who ran Citicorp Venture Capital in London, Schroder Ventures (now Permira) and Apax's buy-out group before founding Alchemy (1997) and turnaround fund Better Capital (2009). Now Guernsey-based, he invests privately via the Perscitus family office and writes a regular column.
interesting_fact: He named Better Capital after apologising to Alchemy investors for 'too many investment and people errors' and promising to invest again 'but better'.
deep_cut_fact: A Lancaster chemistry graduate (honorary doctorate 2022), his Jon Moulton Charity Trust funds non-commercial clinical trials - 170+ trials and about £53m committed so far, yielding 100+ published papers.
notes: Famously outspoken and media-friendly (frequent commentator, writes 'Jon Moulton's Diary'-style columns hosted on the Perscitus site) - a good podcast prospect. Perscitus has an EA to the principal; route via info@ inbox.

name: Marc Worth
profile: Co-founder (with brother Julian) of fashion trend-forecaster WGSN, sold to Emap for £140m in 2005, and later founder of Stylus. Died of a heart attack on 13 January 2023, aged 61.
notes: DECEASED 13 Jan 2023 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Worth). Rich-list entry was shared with brother Julian Worth, who could be researched separately if relevant.

name: Arokiaswamy Velumani
current_role: Founder, Thyrocare Technologies; founder of Nueclear Healthcare (PET-CT cancer imaging), Navi Mumbai; investor and mentor
profile: A. Velumani (b. 1959) grew up in a landless farming family near Coimbatore, spent 14 years at India's Bhabha Atomic Research Centre and in 1996 founded Thyrocare, a low-cost, franchise-fed central-lab diagnostics chain that listed in 2016. In 2021 PharmEasy's parent bought a 66.1% controlling stake; he now focuses on Nueclear Healthcare and is a prominent mentor-commentator for founders.
interesting_fact: Thyrocare's April 2016 IPO was oversubscribed 72.86 times, and the 2021 PharmEasy deal made it the first Indian listed company acquired by a startup.
deep_cut_fact: His first job, in 1979, was as a shift chemist at Gemini Capsules, a small Coimbatore pharma firm that shut down after three years; he then joined BARC as a lab assistant and earned his PhD in thyroid biochemistry (1995) while working there.
notes: Very accessible public figure: active on social media and gives many talks/interviews about frugal entrepreneurship - strong podcast prospect. His personal site is JS-only so no handles could be extracted; verify his X account from the site before use (web search budget was exhausted).

name: Rupert Hambro
profile: British banker (Hambros Bank chairman 1983-86; co-founder of J O Hambro Capital Management; Hambro Perks co-founder) who died on 19 February 2021, aged 77.
notes: DECEASED 19 Feb 2021 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rupert_Hambro). Sunday Times 2020 entry predates his death.

name: Anton Bilton
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Deputy Chairman, The Raven Property Group (formerly Raven Russia); non-executive Chairman, Sabina Estates (Ibiza)
profile: Anton Bilton is a third-generation British property developer who co-founded Raven Russia (now The Raven Property Group), which built a large portfolio of Russian logistics warehouses, and has founded three other AIM-floated companies. He chairs Sabina Estates, a luxury-villa development on Ibiza, and funds consciousness/psychedelics research.
interesting_fact: After a mystical experience at 15, he co-founded the Tyringham Initiative in 2015, hosting multidisciplinary symposia on DMT research at his Buckinghamshire home; its documentary 'ENTITIES' completes production in 2026. He also wrote a novel, 'Soul Searcher', about a Wall Street LBO dealmaker's near-death experience.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded the UK charity Standing Voice, which supports people with albinism in Tanzania and East Africa, and through the Bilton Charitable Foundation helped establish The Bilton High School in Hlabekisa, South Africa.
notes: Unusually open public persona (own website, blog, book, documentary) - good prospect, best via his site's contact form. Raven's Russian warehouse business is a sensitive topic post-2022; the Raven role on his site may be dated. Do not confuse with the unrelated US 'RAVEN Property Group' (Pacific Northwest).

name: Madhukar Reddy Gangadi
current_role: Founder, Managing Director and CEO, MedPlus Health Services Ltd (NSE/BSE listed), Hyderabad
profile: Dr Gangadi Madhukar Reddy, a medical doctor with a Wharton MBA, founded Hyderabad-based MedPlus in 2006 to build a trusted pharmacy chain using technology to cut supply-chain inefficiency. It is now India's second-largest pharmacy chain with 5,500+ stores in 800+ cities, plus diagnostics, private-label manufacturing and e-pharmacy, and listed via a December 2021 IPO.
interesting_fact: MedPlus initially traded under the 'Aushadhi' brand and was renamed MedPlus after its first 48 stores; it retreated from Gujarat and Rajasthan in 2007 before relaunching in Ahmedabad in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a doctor (MBBS, Sri Venkateswara University) before his Wharton MBA, and has been a director of MedPlus since its incorporation on 30 November 2006; his COO is a former laparoscopic surgeon from Nellore who studied at the same university.
notes: Gives TV interviews (e.g. ABN 'Best In The Business'). No IR email found on the corporate site; the company secretary contact in exchange filings is an alternative. marketing@ is a corporate department inbox, not personal.

name: Dinesh Kumar Himatsingka
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Himatsingka Seide Ltd (Bengaluru)
profile: D.K. Himatsingka founded Himatsingka Seide, a Bengaluru-based vertically integrated home-textiles group (bedding, bath, drapery and upholstery fabrics) that sells in 30+ countries through 15+ owned and licensed brands. The company credits him with pioneering luxury home-textile manufacturing in India; day-to-day leadership now sits with Executive Vice Chairman & MD Shrikant Himatsingka.
interesting_fact: Himatsingka reports 99.1% water recovery at its zero-liquid-discharge manufacturing facilities and a workforce of 10,000+ associates.
notes: Low personal media profile; company-level contact only (IR mailbox handled by the Company Secretary). Web search budget ran out before a sourced deep-cut fact could be found.

name: Rajarathinam Nadar
current_role: Head of Super Saravana Stores (flagship Saravana Stores entity), Chennai
profile: S. Rajarathinam Nadar co-founded Saravana Stores in 1969 with brothers S. Yogarathinam and S. Selvarathinam, migrants from Panika Nadar Kudiyiruppu village near Tuticorin. The family chain - Tamil Nadu's largest family-owned retailer, turnover about ₹2,500 crore - later split into separate entities; he runs the flagship 'Super Saravana Stores' (T. Nagar, Purasawalkam, Porur, Chromepet, Madurai, Coimbatore).
interesting_fact: The business began as 'Shanmugam Stores', a small shop selling vessels; the first 'Saravana Stores' complex opened on T. Nagar's Ranganathan Street in 1977. The company site credits Shri Rajaratnam's motto 'Quality and trust should always be accessible to all.'
deep_cut_fact: The Saravana group launched its own 100% milk-based ice-cream brand, Jamaai, in 2004, made at a factory in Padappai on the Sriperumbudur road.
notes: Social accounts are the company's, not his personal ones. Very private, traditional family business; outreach in Tamil via the store office is likely needed. Do not confuse with nephew 'Legend' Saravanan, who runs the separate Legend New Saravana Stores. Current age/health and alive status not verified (search budget exhausted).

name: Ross M Cummings
current_role: Trustee of family trusts that held ~11.6% of Sterling Check Corp. (filing address c/o Bluewater Systems, Austin, TX)
profile: SEC filings show Ross M. Cummings reported as a 10%+ holder of background-screening firm Sterling Check Corp. (IPO 2021; acquired by First Advantage in 2024) solely in his capacity as trustee of three family trusts linked to Sterling's founding Greenblatt family, with sole voting/dispositive power over 11.07m shares. He does not appear to be the economic owner of that stake.
notes: Likely a FALSE POSITIVE for a UHNW list: the ~$189m is trust assets he controls as trustee, not his own wealth (Schedule 13G, 14 Feb 2022: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1645070/000119312522039906/d316664dsc13g.htm). No public bio or contact found. Recommend dropping.
